messages:
maria: heads up — noticed last night's EU shard had ~2k late events concentrated in 3 tiny 10-15m windows. we can probably avoid a full backfill if we do opportunistic mini-window reprocesses
jon: can you paste the window ranges?
maria: sure: 2026-03-20T23:10-23:25Z, 23:40-23:50Z, 00:05-00:20Z. mostly small customer cohorts hitting delayed ingestion.
reza: +1 for mini windows. big backfills spike costs and steal dedicated slots. how confident are we that recomputing those windows won't break aggregates?
maria: prototype dry-run on staging looked fine — aggregates delta <0.01% for the affected metrics. but we need routing/quotas decision: prefer doing these on Dedicated pool or piggyback on Shared?
tara: from console/ops perspective, piggybacking on Shared is risky during peak. we should prefer Dedicated capacity if available and fall back to Shared with rate limit. also we need an operator flag in console to mark a window as "operator-approved" so SLAs can override auto-skips.
jon: agree. propose policy: prefer=deds, fallback=shared-rate-limited, max-concurrency=4, dry-run first, then commit after ops thumbs-up.
maria: sketch of CLI for dry-run I used:
```
reprocess 
  --region eu 
  --window "2026-03-20T23:10Z/2026-03-20T23:25Z" 
  --prefer dedicated 
  --dry-run 
  --max-concurrency 2
```
ops-bot: NOTICE: scheduled dry-run job created (job_id: eu-mini-1123) — status: queued
sam: what about console UX? do we surface the staging dry-run delta and let ops accept?
tara: yes, add a small panel: "dry-run summary" with delta %, token-cost estimate, and a toggle "apply recompute". also show which pool it will use and the fallback rules.
reza: quota question — if we prefer Dedicated but the tenant doesn't have reserved capacity, should we auto-bid for burst slot or route to shared?
jon: we currently allow burst for prod tenants with billing-commit level >= X. otherwise route to shared. we can add an opt-in flag to let owners allow burst for these mini-windows.
maria: one more safety: run a post-check alert if aggregates changed by >0.5% and auto-roll back by producing a compensating correction? probably just alert and mark the recompute as suspect for manual review.
ops-bot: ALERT RULE SUGGESTION: notify #incidents if recompute_delta > 0.5% for any top-level agg in eu shard within 30m of run completion
sam: cc @product — this affects rollout UX for the console. we should avoid adding too many clicks but still keep safeguards.
tara: maybe default to auto-apply for <=0.05% delta and require manual apply above that up to 0.5%.
reza: sounds reasonable. can we add a shallow validation step to fail fast: compute diff on sample subset before launching full recompute?
maria: done in the dry-run flow already — the dry-run currently samples 2% of keys for speed. need to document sample size and confidence.
jon: next steps: (1) add routing policy hook `prefer=deds, fallback=shared:rate(100r/s)` (2) console: dry-run panel + apply toggle + burst opt-in flag (3) ops-bot rule for >0.5% alerts (4) run a small EU dry-run tonight and report results
maria: I'll schedule dry-run at 02:30 UTC and post results here. tagging @oncall in case it surfaces anything noisy. :eyes:
ops-bot: REMINDER: oncall tagged (team: eng-sre) — please monitor recompute job eu-mini-1123 at 02:30 UTC
sam: thanks — keep notes on cost uplift per window so we can tune thresholds.
maria: will do. thanks everyone.
